response.rationale: R1 uniquely integrates the patient's sickle cell disease with pathognomonic retinal findings (black sunburst lesions, ischemic macular whitening, abnormal capillary bed) and OCT evidence of middle retinal layer atrophy, directly matching the diagnosis. R4 is contradicted by the explicit absence of a cherry-red spot and other typical CRAO features. R2 lacks any diabetes history and its support is a nonspecific capillary abnormality also seen in sickle cell retinopathy. R1 is the only candidate with no raw contradictions and full syndromic coherence.

rejected.why: Absence of cherry-red spot, hemorrhage, and neovascularization directly contradicts central retinal artery occlusion; the ischemic whitening is also explained by sickle cell vaso-occlusion.
